analysis.summary: The PR migrates the infrastructure to SST but introduces a critical authentication failure in the BFF, a functional regression by dropping campaign tracking, and potential runtime environment mismatches in the client-side integrator.

bugs.title: BFF Authentication failure due to missing API key header
bugs.description: BFF handlers are updated to require a static 'x-api-key' header (Config.ENDPOINT_DIRECTORY_API_KEY) for verification. However, the client-side Integrator and Feature App do not send this header, and the SST infrastructure (CloudFront) in stacks/Site.ts does not inject it into origin requests.
bugs.risk: All runtime requests from the frontend to the BFF (app-model and post-form) will fail with 401 Unauthorized errors, breaking the entire application functionality.
bugs.codeSnippet:
logger,
-    staticVerifySecret: process.env.STATIC_VERIFY_SECRET,
+    staticVerifySecret: JSON.stringify({
+      headerName: `x-api-key`,
+      headerValue: Config.ENDPOINT_DIRECTORY_API_KEY,
+    }),

bugs.title: Regression: campaignId parameter lost in Integrator rewrite
bugs.description: The previous server-side integrator correctly extracted 'campaignId' from query parameters and passed it to the Feature App config. The new client-side rewrite completely omits 'campaignId' logic.
bugs.risk: Marketing attribution and specific campaign-based form behaviors in the Connectivity (PCP) domain will fail to function, as the Feature App will no longer receive the necessary tracking ID.

bugs.title: Environment name mismatch in client-side integrator
bugs.description: The integrator's 'envName' logic defaults to 'dev' and only checks URL search params. Unlike the 'target' variable, it does not fall back to 'process.env.TARGET' injected by Webpack.
bugs.risk: In environments like stage or prod, if the URL parameter is missing, the app will initialize with 'dev' settings. This causes the Feature App to attempt to resolve endpoints or feature flags for the wrong environment, leading to CORS errors or incorrect business logic.

notBugs.reason: The split('/') logic in the OriginRewrite edge lambda is a standard pattern for these feature apps to resolve domain names based on URI segments; it is consistent with the established deployment architecture.
Routing 'post-form' through '__app-private__' is an intentional design choice to differentiate public asset requests from sensitive API submissions, even if both currently target the same BFF origin.

While defaulting to 'forms-app' in some fallbacks vs 'esign-app' in SST config is inconsistent, the production bundle injected via Webpack's DefinePlugin (process.env.BASE_URL) will take precedence, mitigating runtime impact.
